record.paper_title: Periods of Integrals on Algebraic Manifolds: Summary of Main Results and Discussion of Open Problems
record.original_question: For a period mapping from a smooth algebraic family whose period matrix domain D is a bounded domain and whose arithmetic monodromy quotient is D/T, does Borel's extension theorem remain valid for smooth compactifications of the base whose boundary is not assumed to have normal crossings? Equivalently, in what sense is D/T minimal at infinity independently of the chosen smooth compactification?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $f: X \to S$ be a smooth projective family of complex algebraic varieties over a smooth quasi-projective base $S$, and consider the associated period mapping
$$\Phi: S \to D/\Gamma,$$
where $D$ is the classifying domain (assumed here to be a bounded symmetric / Hermitian symmetric domain in the classical case, or more generally a period domain admitting a bounded realization) parametrizing polarized Hodge structures of the relevant type, and $\Gamma$ is the arithmetic monodromy group acting properly discontinuously on $D$. Borel's extension theorem asserts that if $\bar S$ is a smooth projective compactification of $S$ such that the boundary $\bar S \setminus S$ is a normal crossings divisor, then $\Phi$ extends to a morphism $\bar\Phi: \bar S \to \overline{D/\Gamma}$, where $\overline{D/\Gamma}$ denotes a canonical (e.g., Baily–Borel) compactification of $D/\Gamma$.

Question: Does the extension property continue to hold for an arbitrary smooth projective compactification $\bar S$ of $S$ whose boundary $\bar S \setminus S$ is not assumed to have normal crossings? Equivalently, characterize the precise sense in which $D/\Gamma$ is "minimal at infinity": namely, show that there is a canonical compactification of $D/\Gamma$ to which every period map from a smooth quasi-projective $S$ extends, independently of the choice of smooth compactification of $S$.
artifact.status_search_result: Recent work (Bakker–Brunebarbe–Tsimerman and follow-ups, 2020–2025) constructs functorial proper/projective compactifications of period images using o-minimal GAGA and establishes extension results that go well beyond the classical Borel theorem. In particular, a canonical Baily–Borel-type compactification of the image of a period map exists, providing a notion of minimality at infinity, although full results for arbitrary smooth compactifications of the base without normal crossings assumptions are part of ongoing research.

status_evidence.title: Baily–Borel compactifications of period images
status_evidence.snippet: Constructs a functorial projective compactification for period images; morphisms extend from log smooth algebraic spaces.
status_evidence.claim: Provides canonical compactification realizing minimality at infinity for period images.

status_evidence.title: Analog of Satake-Baily-Borel for period maps
status_evidence.snippet: Functorial compactification of the image of a period map of a polarizable integral pure VHS, with ample Griffiths bundle.
status_evidence.claim: Generalizes Borel's extension beyond the classical Hermitian symmetric setting.

status_evidence.title: On the generalized toroidal completion of period mappings
status_evidence.snippet: Recent extension/completion results for period mappings.
status_evidence.claim: Active progress on extension theorems for period maps without normal crossings assumptions.
